body:
**Claimed by the `domain:ui` PM seat (`os-tesla`) — dispatched to an `os-dev` seat this round.**

Claimed: objectui#9357 — `UseNavigationOverlayOptions.onRowClick` understates its arity and the hook casts the understatement away
Clause-②: yes

## Premise verified against the tree before dispatch

`origin/main`, `packages/react/src/hooks/useNavigationOverlay.ts` — both halves, byte-for-byte:

```
:142    /** External onRowClick callback — if set, takes full priority */
:143    onRowClick?: (record: Record<string, unknown>) => void;

:265    // External onRowClick takes full priority. Forward the modifier event
:268    if (onRowClick) {
:269      (onRowClick as (r: Record<string, unknown>, e?: HandleClickModifiers) => void)(record, event);
```

The declaration says one parameter; the call site casts the declaration away to pass two. ⇒ the cast is the tell, and it is **in the same file, 126 lines apart**.

## Why this one is the root and not another instance

It was found while implementing objectui#9341, which repaired a **symptom**: an `object-kanban` board called an authored `onCardClick` twice, and the surviving channel turned out to deliver `(record, event)` where the published type promised `(card)`. Every consumer copies the understated spelling — `ObjectKanbanComponentProps.onRowClick`, `ObjectGallery`'s pair, `KanbanRendererProps.schema.onCardClick` — and `ObjectView` already **works around it**, spelling its second parameter optional at three call sites.

⇒ A workaround at three call sites plus a cast at the source is a declaration that lost an argument, not a family of independent bugs.

`Clause-②: yes`: widening `onRowClick` to declare the second parameter moves a published type in `@object-ui/react`. My reading — ⭐ offered as a prediction to falsify — is that it is source-compatible in **both** directions, because a one-argument handler stays assignable to a two-argument optional signature; the objectui#9341 seat measured exactly that for the sibling key and found it stronger than predicted. ⛔ Measure it here rather than inheriting it.

`tsconfig.base.json` sets `removeComments: false` and `packages/react` builds with plain `tsc`, so that block ships verbatim into `dist/hooks/useNavigationOverlay.d.ts` — the hover text every consumer reads. The changeset two files away now says the opposite in bold. - The PR body's inherited-red paragraph is **wrong on all three names**: it names *Doc Snippet Type Check* and *Skill Example Check*, both `success` at this head. Live count: 36 checks, 32 success, 3 skipped, **1 failure — `Bundle Analysis`**, 0 cancelled. That one is genuinely inherited (red on `b67b53bc0` and on the `origin/main` tip `e2feb13e1`) and its own bot comment calls it a broken-gauge ceiling verdict, "not a budget violation".
- The PR body was never updated for `d8325fa79` (0 hits for `ts-expect-error`, `TS2322`, `MouseEvent`, `narrower`) and its "Source compatibility" section still asserts "No consumer breaks in either direction", which the probe above refutes at this head.
- Semver stays **`minor`**: the diff is breaking in substance, and `minor` is the only legal declaration here (AGENTS.md line 253 + `check-changeset-no-major.mjs`), whose condition — breaking semantics written out — the changeset body meets. The level is right; the carrier of the compensating prose is what fails.
- PR objectui#9360 carries **no closing keyword** (`Part of objectui#9357`; the card's `closed_by_pull_requests` is `total_count: 0`), so merging it will not close this card. Correct as it stands — the component-prop half stays open.
